title: AAWSAP to AATIP to Elizondo to New York Times chain

tellings.quote: There's a chain you can draw a direct link OSAP to ATIP to to Lu Alzano to New York Times.

plain: There is a direct line, says the national security writer Marik von Rennenkampff, from AAWSAP, a Pentagon-funded study of unexplained aerial reports begun in 2007, to AATIP, a small Pentagon office that studied such reports, to Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official, and then to the New York Times, which made the program public in 2017. He draws this chain on Jesse Michels's show in 2025, in an episode about a debate with a skeptic. His point is that the public story did not come from nowhere but grew out of a real government program.
